papers.title: SpectraViewer
papers.summary: SpectraViewer is a lightweight spectrum browser for quickly opening, viewing, and browsing supported spectrum files, including OPUS native spectrum files, JCAMP-DX files, and DPT data point tables. It is intended for fast visual inspection and navigation through spectrum collections, not for spectral processing or data manipulation.

papers.title: MnemoLink: Curated, injectable personas and artificial memories for AI agents.
papers.summary: MnemoLink is an open-source Python framework and curated registry for modular, injectable personas, episodic memories, and dynamic lego lineages for AI agents, UAVs, robotics, appliances, and BMIs. It decouples experiential context from weights, providing standardized 5-kind memory taxonomy, teleological discovery, and prefix-cache-friendly mnemonic chunks.

papers.title: Rigid-Sync / MASTER OS — Framework Overview and Development Record, Version 1.0
papers.summary: Rigid-Sync / MASTER OS is a proposed relationship-centered physical-operation framework for multi-degree-of-freedom physical systems. This document establishes Version 1.0 of the public framework overview and chronological development record of Rigid-Sync / MASTER OS. The framework originated from Human-Origin movement design and was progressively generalized toward Physical AI, robotics, and multi-DOF control architecture. papers.title: Reflexive Self-Sensing Artificial Tendons
papers.summary: Abstract This work proposes a reflexive self-sensing artificial tendon designed to overcome the limited adaptability and slow recovery of conventional robotic tendons. papers.summary: IMPAC-teen is a synthetic, human-verified dataset of textual social influence scenarios spanning interpersonal and digital settings in an adolescent context. It contains 1,021 texts, 5,100 individual annotation records, and consensus labels for 20 social influence techniques. Of the 1,021 texts, 1,016 texts received annotations from one member of each of five distinct perspectives: late adolescents (aged 18–19), parents, psychologists, communication experts, and teachers.
